title: Versioned gpux releases: one workspace version and one v-tag with release-plz, v1.0.0, release-PR CI, rayx declarations, consumption by git tag

The declared Java directory is packaged with gpux-mobile (listing only).

New group `tools/testkit/tests/release_docs.rs`: the README crate table equals the workspace's packages (directory, package, Rust name; the fork row names all fork packages), and the four install documents show the git-tag form and no crates.io or `../Gpux` form.
Clippy of the one package whose code changes (its new test groups and dev-dependencies), as CLAUDE.md runs it.

`cargo package --workspace` after the manifest changes (version 1.0.0, rayx metadata, new dev-dependency) and before the release, as CLAUDE.md and the packaging rules require; it builds every packaged crate, so it is the compile proof of the version bump. sprints.title: Spike: release-plz gives the workspace one version, one tag and one changelog (scratch clone only)

tasks.title: Prove release-plz's git-only version group in a scratch clone, or switch to the fallback
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Prove d-release-tooling before anything lands. The real checkout does not change in this sprint (its checkpoint reuses the current commit).

1. Install the latest release-plz (`cargo install release-plz --locked`) and record `release-plz --version`; read `release-plz/action@v0.5`'s `action.yml` for a version input.
2. Under ignored `artifacts-temp/agentx/gpux-releases/spike/`: `git clone --no-local <checkout> gpux`, `git init --bare remote.git`, `git -C gpux remote set-url origin <abs>/remote.git`, push `main` there **before** any release-plz command. Pass no GitHub token; no command points at `github.com`.
3. In the scratch clone apply VER-1's edits (version 1.0.0, the 30 requirements, gpui_mobile's inline one), candidate A's `release-plz.toml` and a stub `CHANGELOG.md` with RayX.CLI's header and a `## [1.0.0]` section; commit.
4. Run SPIKE-1's scenarios with `release-plz update` (a release PR's content) and `release-plz release --dry-run` (or a real `release` against the bare remote with `git_release_enable = false` in a scratch-only copy), committing scenario commits with exactly the listed subjects and resetting between scenarios; save each output and `git diff --stat`.
5. If A fails a must-hold scenario, try B; if both fail, tell the owner and switch to fallback C with `amend --specification` (d-release-tooling, d-release-workflow, RPZ-1, RPZ-2, t03), then prove C against the same scenarios.
6. Record in the handoff (`advance --handoff`): the proven `release-plz.toml` text, the release-plz version, the exact files a release PR changes (input of t05), what `update` does on the untagged 1.0.0 tree, whether release-plz compiles anything, and the observations for `docs/releasing.md`.

sprints.title: Release pull requests run only check and package

tasks.title: Recognize a release pull request in the CI planner
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Implement d-release-pr-ci in `.github/actions/plan/plan.sh` from the spike's list of files a release PR changes: after the `ci:` label branch, when `BASE_SHA` is set, a documentation-only change keeps `jobs=(check)` (now including `CHANGELOG.md`); otherwise a release-shaped change sets `jobs=(check package)` and `platforms=(ubuntu)`, before `ci-os:` labels apply. Compare `git show "$BASE_SHA:<file>"` and `git show "$HEAD_SHA:<file>"` with the own version values masked (a file added or deleted is not version-only); keep it portable between GNU and BSD `sed`/`awk` and read the file list whole. Update the script's header comment and `docs/ci.md` (CI-2).

New group `tools/testkit/tests/ci_plan_release_pr.rs` with CI-1's eight cases in temporary git repositories (copy `ci_plan.rs`'s small helpers; `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore = ...)]` with the reason). Then run the existing `ci_plan` group.
